    {
      "id": "SC-01-extraction-window-mixes-scopes",
      "severity": "P3",
      "evidence": [
        "src/service.ts:217",
        "src/service.ts:224",
        "src/service.ts:417",
        "src/service.ts:452",
        "src/service.ts:459"
      ],
      "impact": "extractionGroupKey() keys an extraction window on tenant/space/app/actor/thread but omits `scope`. A multi-turn extracted fact is emitted as `{...baseObservation, text: fact.text}`, so it inherits the scope of the lowest-indexed contributing turn. If one ingest batch mixes scopes for the same actor+thread (e.g. a `workspace` turn at index 0 and an `actor` turn at index 1), a fact synthesised from both is stored at the broader scope, making actor-private (or thread-private) content readable by every actor in the memory space. Bounded: only reachable with MEMORY_EXTRACTOR=llm (off by default); the default PassthroughExtractor emits one fact per turn with text identical to its single source turn, so service.ts:429-433 restores the original observation byte-for-byte and the default write path is unaffected (src/extraction/passthrough-extractor.ts:15). No cross-tenant or cross-space escape, and no read escalation for an attacker, who would have to supply the content in their own batch.",
      "remediation": "Add the resolved scope (`obs.scope ?? \"actor\"`) to extractionGroupKey so a window never mixes visibility loci, or select the narrowest scope/thread among the contributing turns when building the derived observation."
    },
    {
      "id": "SC-02-migration-checksum-claim-unimplemented",
      "severity": "P3",
      "evidence": [
        "docs/CODEX_RUN_SUMMARY.md:176",
        "src/providers/postgres-provider.ts:448",
        "src/providers/postgres-provider.ts:455",
        "migrations/001_init.sql:11",
        "migrations/002_memory_spaces.sql:7"
      ],
      "impact": "The run summary states Postgres migrations are \"ordered, checksummed, and advisory-lock serialized\". Ordering and `pg_advisory_lock` serialization are implemented, but the ledger is `memory_core_migrations(version text PRIMARY KEY, applied_at)` and `migrate()` only tests for the presence of a version row. No digest of the SQL file is stored or compared, so an edited migration whose version already exists is silently skipped and drift is undetectable. This overstates an integrity control in a release-candidate summary; no code path is broken by it.",
      "remediation": "Either drop \"checksummed\" from the summary, or add a `checksum text` column, record a SHA-256 of each applied file, and fail loudly when a recorded version's checksum no longer matches the file on disk."
    },
    {
      "id": "SC-03-get-search-silently-drops-invalid-types",
      "severity": "P3",
      "evidence": [
        "src/http.ts:200",
        "src/http.ts:207",
        "src/http.ts:570",
        "src/http.ts:574"
      ],
      "impact": "On GET /v1/memory/search, parseMemoryTypes() returns `undefined` when the comma list fails `z.array(memoryTypeEnum)`, so `?types=fact,bogus` runs an unfiltered search over every memory type instead of returning 400. The widening stays inside the caller's own authorized visibility (authorizePrincipals still runs at src/http.ts:593), so this is a silent-failure/correctness issue rather than an isolation break, and it diverges from the POST route, where the same value is a validation error.",
      "remediation": "Distinguish \"absent\" from \"unparseable\": when `types` is present but any member fails the enum, surface the ZodError through sendValidationError instead of returning undefined."
    },
    {
      "id": "SC-04-unauthenticated-ready-discloses-provider-internals",
      "severity": "P3",
      "evidence": [
        "src/http.ts:442",
        "src/http.ts:451",
        "src/providers/postgres-provider.ts:1246",
        "src/providers/file-provider.ts:225",
        "src/providers/in-memory-provider.ts:566"
      ],
      "impact": "/ready is served before the /v1 auth middleware and returns the provider's full `detail` string to any caller that can reach the port: Postgres server version and `reltuples` row estimate, embedder model/dimension, vector-failure counters, record/index counts, and the file provider's absolute store path. It also performs a database round trip per request, bounded only by the coarse per-IP limiter. docs/deployment.md:347 correctly states that health/readiness bypass auth, so this is disclosed, but the body is richer than an orchestrator probe needs.",
      "remediation": "Return `{ok, provider}` (kind only) on the unauthenticated path and move `detail` behind an operator credential, or make detail opt-in via configuration; keep the 503 semantics unchanged for readiness."
    },
    {
      "id": "SC-05-pre-auth-limiter-capacity-sheds-new-identities",
      "severity": "P3",
      "evidence": [
        "src/http.ts:313",
        "src/http.ts:335",
        "src/http.ts:337",
        "src/http.ts:436"
      ],
      "impact": "createRateLimiter caps its bucket map at 10,000 entries and answers 429 to any identity that is not already tracked once the cap is reached, rather than evicting. The pre-auth limiter is keyed by `ip:` and applies to every route including /health and /ready, so an IP-rotating flood (or a spoofable X-Forwarded-For chain when MEMORY_TRUST_PROXY_HOPS is set too high) can make a replica reject first-contact requests from legitimate clients and orchestrator probes for up to a 60s window. Authenticated /v1 traffic is keyed by key digest and is bounded by the number of configured credentials, so this does not create a cross-principal read or write.",
      "remediation": "At capacity, evict the oldest bucket (or sweep unconditionally) and admit the new identity instead of returning 429; alternatively exempt /health and /ready from capacity-based rejection so probes cannot be starved."
    },
    {
      "id": "SC-06-hermes-supersede-rejects-server-derived-type-scope",
      "severity": "P3",
      "evidence": [
        "src/integrations/adapters/hermes-plugin/tools.py:117",
        "src/integrations/adapters/hermes-plugin/tools.py:119",
        "src/integrations/adapters/hermes-plugin/tools.py:310"
      ],
      "impact": "supersede() reuses the previous record's `memoryType` and `scope` and passes them through _observation(), which validates against the agent-facing allowlists (_MEMORY_TYPES omits profile/pattern/summary, _SCOPES omits app/tenant). Superseding a record written through REST/SDK with `scope=\"app\"`/`\"tenant\"` or type `profile`/`pattern`/`summary` therefore fails with \"type must be one of ...\"/\"scope must be one of ...\", which is fail-closed but misattributes a server-side condition to the model's arguments. The allowlist itself is correct and required for model-supplied fields (criterion 7 holds).",
      "remediation": "Validate model-supplied values against the allowlists as today, but pass server-derived previous type/scope through unchecked (or map an out-of-allowlist scope to a clear \"this memory cannot be superseded from Hermes\" error)."
    }
